citeAs: Merity, S., Xiong, C., Bradbury, J., and Socher, R. (2016). Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models. arXiv:1609.07843.
creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher (MetaMind - A Salesforce Company)
description: WikiText is a language modeling benchmark dataset constructed from Wikipedia articles that passed the Good or Featured article criteria. It is available in two sizes: WikiText-2 (approximately twice the size of Penn Treebank, ~2M tokens) and WikiText-103 (over 103 million tokens from all extracted articles). Both feature punctuation, original casing, a larger vocabulary, and numbers, and are designed to support evaluation of long-range dependencies and rare word handling.
name: WikiText
rai:dataBiases: The dataset was intentionally constructed from Wikipedia Good and Featured articles (reviewed, well-written, factually accurate, neutral in point of view) to avoid the limitations of Penn Treebank (lower-cased tokens, no punctuation, limited 10k vocabulary). Other large-scale datasets were avoided due to restrictive licensing or randomized sentence ordering (e.g., One Billion Word Benchmark), which is unrealistic for most language use and prevents learning of long-term dependencies.
rai:dataCollection: Articles were selected from Wikipedia that met the Good or Featured article criteria as specified by Wikipedia editors. These articles have been reviewed by humans and are considered well written, factually accurate, broad in coverage, neutral in point of view, and stable. This resulted in 23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles. Text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw text extracted from Wikipedia Good and Featured articles using the Wikipedia API. The raw Wikipedia markup includes macros for metric conversion, abbreviations, language notation, and date handling.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is restricted to Wikipedia articles meeting Good or Featured article criteria, which may not be representative of all language use. The vocabulary excludes words appearing fewer than 3 times, mapping them to <unk>. WikiText-2 has an OoV rate of 2.6% and WikiText-103 has an OoV rate of 0.4%.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Specific sections primarily featuring lists were removed. Minor bugs such as sort keys and Edit buttons that leaked in from HTML were removed. Mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with <formula> tokens. Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer (Koehn et al., 2007), slightly augmented to further split numbers (e.g., 8,600 → 8 @,@ 600). A vocabulary was constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3; words outside the vocabulary were mapped to the <unk> token.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is made freely available to the research community to enable progress on language modeling with realistic vocabularies, rare words, and long-range dependencies. It is intended to serve as a platform to improve handling of rare words and the usage of long-term dependencies in language modeling.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmark dataset for word-level language modeling, particularly for evaluating how well language models can exploit longer contexts, deal with more realistic vocabularies, handle rare words, and learn long-range dependencies. Intended as a replacement for the Penn Treebank for language modeling research.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Moses tokenizer (Koehn et al., 2007) was used for normalization and tokenization, slightly augmented to further split numbers.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: WikiText is a language modeling corpus, not an annotated dataset; no per-item annotation count is discussed.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: No human annotators were used; data was collected from Wikipedia and preprocessed automatically.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No annotation process or inter-annotator agreement is discussed; the dataset is a text corpus without manual annotation.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No annotation platform used; data was collected from Wikipedia automatically.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No manual annotation protocol; the dataset is a text corpus collected and preprocessed automatically.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No discussion of missing data handling beyond standard preprocessing steps.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe for data collection from Wikipedia is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation of missing values described; out-of-vocabulary words are mapped to <unk> as part of preprocessing, not imputation.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation (augmentation, balancing, resampling) described for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No discussion of personal or sensitive information in the dataset; it is a Wikipedia text corpus.
